title: Six weeks in
setting: Somebody who has been training for six weeks and can't feel the difference.

lines.t: Six weeks with a personal trainer and I still can't run for the bus.
How many times a week are you working out?
Twice, more or less.
Twice is where you keep fit. Three times is where you get in shape.
I was badly out of shape in January.
You were, and you aren't now. Your endurance has doubled and you haven't noticed.
It doesn't feel like it.
It never does from the inside. How many reps on the last set?
Twelve. In January it was six.
There's your answer. Do you warm up properly?
Five minutes, usually.
Ten, and cool down for five afterwards. That's where people your age stop getting injured.
And if I want to build muscle rather than only lift weights?
Heavier, fewer reps, and eat properly. Stamina comes from the running, and the two don't fight each other.

title: Before the final
setting: A coach talks to the team before a match everyone expects them to lose.

lines.t: They beat us four nil in November.
They did. Every newspaper has already picked them.
That's not helping.
It should. They have to win. We only have to play.
And if they score first?
Then we're where everyone expects us to be, and nothing has changed.
Home advantage is theirs too.
For ninety minutes it's eleven against eleven and a referee.
You really think we can do this.
I think underdogs play better without pressure. Go and enjoy it.

title: Two-all at eighty-nine
setting: Two friends the morning after a match that ended level.

lines.t: Did you see it?
Two-all, I heard.
They equalised in the eighty-ninth minute.
So it's a draw.
A draw that feels like a loss. We were the underdog and we nearly won.
Better than last month, when they thrashed you five-nil.
Don't remind me.
Where does that leave the league table?
Fourth. Two points behind, and the runner-up place is still possible.
Who scored?
Kolev, twice. That's his personal best for a season, and it's only March.
Then a narrow win on Saturday and you beat them on goal difference.

title: I gave it up at nineteen
setting: One friend tries to get another back into a sport she stopped playing.

lines.t: Did you ever play anything seriously?
Volleyball, until I was nineteen. Then I gave it up.
Why?
University, a job, the usual reasons people stop.
Would you take up a sport again?
At forty-three? Everybody there would be twenty.
There's a league on Tuesdays where the youngest player is thirty-eight.
That changes it.
It's a level playing field once nobody can jump any more.
Then send me the details before I talk myself out of it.

title: Nine men and thirty minutes
setting: Planning for an away match with two players missing.

lines.t: Who's in the line-up on Saturday?
The same eleven, if Kolev is fit.
And the rest of the squad?
Two are out injured, one is suspended after being sent off last week.
That foul was never a red card.
The referee thought otherwise and nobody asked us.
It's an away game, so we'll be under pressure from kick-off.
Without home advantage, and their ground holds twelve thousand.
Then we train hard on Thursday, and I'll coach the back four myself.
And if it goes to extra time?
Then the fitness work in January pays for itself.
There's a warm-up match on Tuesday against the under-21s.
Use it. Everybody plays forty-five minutes and nobody gets hurt. Keep it level until half-time and the crowd turns on them.
I'll confirm the fixture with them this afternoon.

title: Six weeks off
setting: A physiotherapist explains an injury to a runner.

lines.t: How bad is it? I've got a race in October.
You've sprained the ankle. Six weeks, no running.
Six weeks? I haven't missed a session in two years.
I know. That's part of why it happened.
So I just sit still?
No. Swimming from week two, and upper body from tomorrow.
That's not really training.
It's training the parts you've ignored for years.
And October?
Possible, if you treat rest as part of the plan, not a break from it.

title: Three weeks, not three days
setting: The same leg, injured twice in two months.

lines.t: I pulled a muscle on Saturday.
Which one?
The back of the thigh. And I sprained my ankle in February.
Same leg?
Same leg.
Then you aren't resting enough. How many rest days a week?
One, if I remember.
Two, and they go in the calendar like a meeting. People who train seven days burn out by June.
How long am I out for?
Three weeks, and you'll want to come back after ten days. Recover properly or you'll be out injured again in April.

title: The season ticket
setting: One friend goes to the stadium, the other watches at home.

lines.t: I've had a season ticket for nine years.
Even when they were terrible?
Especially then. You support a team, you don't rent it.
I usually just catch the game on television.
It's a different thing in the stadium. You can hear what the players shout at each other.
And when you can't go?
I watch the highlights at eleven and pretend I don't know the result.
Does that work?
Somebody always texts me. Every supporter has one friend who ruins it.
Then put your phone away for ninety minutes, the way you do in the stadium.
